content:
As WhatsApp gears up to officially launch its username feature, users can now save a contact's username alongside their name and phone number. Details below.

The ability to include a username field when adding new contacts has begun rolling out to some WhatsApp users.

While usernames have long been a staple on most messaging platforms, WhatsApp has only recently started moving away from relying solely on phone numbers to identify users.

WhatsApp had previously rolled out a username reservation system, allowing users to lock in their desired handle ahead of the feature's official launch to prevent impersonation by scammers.

A few weeks ago, WhatsApp began enabling the username feature for some iPhone users.

Now, according to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp has started adding a username field when users add a new contact. The field appears between the name field and the phone number field.

Here's what WABetaInfo had to say:

As noted by WABetaInfo, this username field appears to be rolling out to some users on both the beta and stable versions of WhatsApp.

When testing on the latest stable version, the field appeared, but even when entering a real, existing username, the system still showed a message saying "this username is not on WhatsApp."

Still, this is undoubtedly another step forward for WhatsApp as it catches up to its competitors, adding a basic feature that many felt should have been there long ago.
